label: pre-commit runs twelve blocking gate families in one script, and four of them (route-remint, contract-recompile, spec-remint, doc-version-bump) re-mint and stage files during the hook instead of only checking.

Two expensive commit-path checks were already removed for the block-or-drop reason: the doc-model reference validator moved to CI and the report-only pre-push test suites cost 40 s per push before removal.
The cheap gates are cheap: comment hygiene takes 0.20 s on 40 TypeScript files and compiled-route-guard takes 0.07 s across all hubs, so hook cost concentrates in the re-mint engines.
pre-push still carries an advisory skill-root metadata check that warns and never blocks, the same non-blocking shape as the checks already moved to CI.
The gate switch surface is 15 rows in gates.tsv with 10 persistable pre-commit gates, and the hook test suite is about 170 KB of shell with pre-commit.test.sh at 67 KB.
The source-root and trust preamble is duplicated in every hook script, and source-root-selection.test.sh exists to assert the copies stay identical rather than to test a shared library.
